To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
doctors and nurses in cancer units are emotionally affected by communicating with patients and that this affects their interactions with patients.

(1) Doctors and nurses in cancer care experience considerable psychosocial strain in their daily patient interactions; (2) This is managed by adopting strategies that allow them to retain a sense of control and maintain a professional identity; (3) These strategies include managing patients and managing self to keep negative emotions at bay; (4) Most staff believe that their communication skills are sufficient;

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study found that doctors and nurses working in cancer units have to deal with emotional issues on a daily basis and that the strategies they use to deal with these issues are not necessarily the best ones.
communication with cancer patients is an emotionally stressful experience for doctors and nurses that requires a variety of strategies to manage this stress.
the emotional burden of caring for cancer patients is a key issue in the communication process and that this needs to be recognized by health care providers and health care organizations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
doctors and nurses are not trained to manage the emotional impact of their daily encounters with cancer patients.
doctors and nurses working in cancer care need a safe space in which to reflect on and share their experiences of working with cancer patients.
the doctors and nurses in this study were able to manage their emotional strain in their work with cancer patients by managing the patients and by managing themselves.
The main takeaway from our work is that

communication training programs should include strategies that support staff in managing their own emotions, as well as those of patients, in order to improve the quality of communication in cancer care.

the emotional strain of communicating with patients in a cancer unit is considerable, but the strategies that doctors and nurses use to cope with it can be understood and addressed in training programs.
we need to be mindful of the emotional strain on the staff in the cancer unit.
